title: Where Is It?
objectives: I can say where something is with under, beside, between, behind, and inside.
I can follow directions that use position words.
I can hide a toy and tell a partner where it is.
rationale: Position words let children say where things are and follow classroom directions, so they are some of the most reusable words in kindergarten. All five are prepositions, taught with a toy and a box so children see and act out each one. Between and inside need two things or a closed space, so they come after the simpler under, beside, and behind. The unit builds on ready and listen from unit 1, because children must listen to a direction and be ready to move.

passage.title: Pip Plays Hide-and-Seek
paras: Pip the puppy plays hide-and-seek with Mia. He hides under the bed, but his tail sticks out.
He runs behind the couch, but Mia still sees his ears.
At last Pip squeezes inside a big box. The box sits between two chairs, and Mia cannot find him. Pip peeks out and sits beside her.

qs.q: In the story, where is the box that Pip hides inside?
qs.why: The box sits between two chairs.

qs.q: Where does Mia still see Pip's ears?
qs.why: Pip runs behind the couch, but Mia still sees his ears.

qs.q: Where does Pip sit at the end?
qs.why: Pip peeks out and sits beside Mia.

write.prompt: Pick a toy and tell a partner where you would hide it. Use one position word. You can draw it too.

study.task: Show each position word with a toy and a box: under, beside, between, behind, inside. Say the word each time you move the toy.

teacher.overview: Children learn five position words by moving a toy and a box, then hear them in a hide-and-seek read-aloud and use them to give directions. Everything is spoken and acted out; children do not read or write.

notes.va.under.prep: Teach with a toy and a table. The key idea is below, not on top. Children often say under for anything near an object, so check with the toy each time.
notes.va.beside.prep: Show with two chairs and two children, then with two blocks. Beside means touching or very close at the side; if the toy is far away, it is not beside.
notes.va.between.prep: Needs two things. Set up two blocks and move a toy to the middle. Children often use between with only one object, so always name both things.
notes.va.behind.prep: Use a child and a screen or a big book. Behind is at the back from where you stand, so turn the toy around to show it can change.
notes.va.inside.prep: Use a box with a lid. Inside means closed in; a toy standing near a box is not inside. Pair with outside so children see the contrast.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I will put my bear under the table. It is lower than the table, so it is under. Now I will put it beside the chair, close at the side. Say it with me: the bear is beside the chair.'
discuss: Can the same toy be under and beside something? Show me.
Why do we need position words when we play a hiding game?
misconceptions: Under and behind mean the same thing.
Beside means anywhere in the room.
extend: Play Simon Says with position words using a chair and a bear.
Make a class book: each child draws a toy and writes one position word with teacher help.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit ready and listen by giving two-step position directions. Use under, between, and inside again in unit 4 when children sort objects, and use behind and under in unit 6 action words.

wida.oral: Partner A hides a small toy under a cup, behind a book, or inside a bag. Partner B guesses with a position word, such as 'It is under the cup,' until the toy is found.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (debajo de, al lado de, entre, detrás de, dentro de) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; prepositions often need the phrase, not one word.
Sense boundary: between is taught only as a position word (in the middle of two things), not as a choice between options.
Sense boundary: inside is taught as a preposition; the noun and adjective senses are left out.
